privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy describes how ft_transcendence ("the Service", "we", "us") collects, uses, and protects your personal data when you use our Pong web application.

s1.heading: 1. Who We Are
s1.body: ft_transcendence is a student project developed as part of the 42 School curriculum. It is not a commercial product. Contact:

s2.heading: 2. Data We Collect

rows: Google, if you choose OAuth login

s2.outro: We do not collect payment information, and we do not sell or share your data with third parties for advertising.

s3.heading: 3. How We Store Your Data
list: Passwords are hashed and never stored in plain text.
Avatars are stored as encoded data in our database.
Data is stored in a PostgreSQL database running within our Docker-based infrastructure.
Access tokens (JWT) authenticate requests and are short-lived; refresh tokens are rotated on use.

s4.heading: 4. Legal Basis & Purpose of Processing
list: Provide core account and gameplay functionality (contract necessity).
Secure your account (legitimate interest).
Enable optional features you opt into, such as OAuth login (consent).

s5.heading: 5. Your Rights
s5.intro: Under GDPR and similar frameworks, you have the right to:
list: Access the personal data we hold about you.
Rectify inaccurate data, e.g. via your profile settings.
Erase your account and associated data ("right to be forgotten").
Export your data in a portable format.
Object to or restrict certain processing.

s6.heading: 6. Data Retention
s6.body: We retain your account data for as long as your account is active. If you delete your account, your personal data is removed from our active database within 7 business days, except where retention is required for legitimate security logging.

s7.heading: 7. Third-Party Services
s7.body: If you log in via Google OAuth, Google's own privacy policy governs the data they process on their end. We only receive the profile fields necessary to create or link your account: name, email, avatar.

s8.heading: 8. Cookies & Local Storage
s8.body: We use tokens stored client-side solely to keep you logged in. We do not use tracking or advertising cookies.

s9.heading: 9. Children's Privacy
s9.body: Our Service is not intended for or directed to children under the age of 13. We do not knowingly collect or solicit personal information from anyone under 13. If we discover that a child under 13 has registered and provided us with personal data, we will delete their account and wipe their information from our databases immediately. If you believe that a child under 13 has provided data to us, please contact us immediately.

s10.heading: 10. Changes to This Policy
s10.body: We may update this policy as the project evolves. Material changes will be noted with an updated "Last updated" date.

s11.heading: 11. Contact
s11.pre: Questions about this policy or your data:

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: Welcome to ft_transcendence ("the Service"). By creating an account or using the Service, you agree to these Terms of Service ("Terms"). This is a student project built for the 42 School curriculum and is provided for educational and demonstration purposes.

s1.heading: 1. Eligibility
s1.body: You must be at least 13 years old to create an account. By registering, you confirm that the information you provide is accurate.

s2.heading: 2. Your Account
list: You are responsible for keeping your login credentials confidential.
You are responsible for all activity that occurs under your account.
You may log in via email/password or Google OAuth.
You may delete your account at any time by contacting us.

s3.heading: 3. Acceptable Use
list: Use the Service to harass, abuse, or harm other users.
Attempt to disrupt, exploit, or gain unauthorized access to the Service, its infrastructure, or other users' accounts, including cheating or exploiting bugs.
Upload avatars or content that is illegal, offensive, or infringes on others' rights.
Use automated tools (bots) to play matches or manipulate leaderboards, unless explicitly playing against the provided AI opponent feature.
s3.outro: We reserve the right to suspend or delete accounts that violate these Terms.

s4.heading: 4. Content You Provide
list: You retain ownership of content you upload, e.g. your avatar.
By uploading an avatar, you grant us a limited license to store and display it within the Service.
You are responsible for ensuring you have the right to upload any content you submit.

s5.heading: 5. Game Data & Fair Play
s5.body: Match history, stats, and tournament results are recorded based on actual gameplay through the Service. We may reset, wipe, or modify game data during development without notice, as this is an actively developed student project.

s6.heading: 6. Availability
s6.body: This Service is a student project and is provided "as is", without warranties of any kind, express or implied. We do not guarantee continuous uptime, that the Service will be free of bugs or errors, or long-term data preservation beyond the project's active development or grading period.

s7.heading: 7. Limitation of Liability
s7.body: To the fullest extent permitted by law, the developers of ft_transcendence are not liable for any indirect, incidental, or consequential damages arising from your use of the Service. This Service is not intended for production or commercial use.

s8.heading: 8. Third-Party Login
s8.body: If you choose to log in via Google OAuth, your use of that login method is also subject to Google's own Terms of Service.

s9.heading: 9. Termination
s9.body: We may suspend or terminate your access to the Service at any time, with or without cause, including for violations of these Terms.

s10.heading: 10. Changes to These Terms
s10.body: We may revise these Terms as the project evolves. Continued use of the Service after changes constitutes acceptance of the revised Terms.

s11.heading: 11. Governing Context
s11.body: This project is developed as part of the 42 School curriculum and these Terms are intended for that educational context rather than as a commercially enforceable agreement.
